metadata.title: Noise-Contrastive Estimation: A New Estimation Principle for Unnormalized Statistical Models (Gutmann & Hyvarinen, 2010)
metadata.framework: Estimating parameters of unnormalized probabilistic models by training a classifier to distinguish data from artificially generated noise
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Gutmann & Hyvarinen (2010). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: Unnormalized statistical model
nodes.statement: A statistical model $p_m(\mathbf{x}; \theta) = \frac{1}{Z(\theta)} p^0_m(\mathbf{x}; \theta)$ where $p^0_m$ is an unnormalized density and $Z(\theta) = \int p^0_m(\mathbf{x}; \theta) d\mathbf{x}$ is the intractable partition function. The goal is to estimate $\theta$ without computing $Z(\theta)$.

nodes.name: Noise distribution
nodes.statement: A fixed, known noise distribution $p_n(\mathbf{x})$ from which noise samples can be easily drawn. For each data sample $\mathbf{x}$ from $p_d$ (the data distribution), $\nu$ noise samples are drawn from $p_n$.

nodes.name: NCE objective function
nodes.statement: Treat estimation as binary classification: assign label $C=1$ to data and $C=0$ to noise. The NCE objective maximizes: $J_T(\theta) = \frac{1}{T_d} \sum_{t=1}^{T_d} \log h(\mathbf{x}_t; \theta) + \frac{1}{T_n} \sum_{t=1}^{T_n} \log(1 - h(\mathbf{y}_t; \theta))$ where $h(\mathbf{x}; \theta) = \frac{p_m(\mathbf{x}; \theta)}{p_m(\mathbf{x}; \theta) + \nu \cdot p_n(\mathbf{x})}$ is the posterior probability that $\mathbf{x}$ is data (not noise), treating $\log Z(\theta)$ as a parameter $c$ to be estimated.

nodes.name: Consistency of NCE
nodes.statement: As $T \to \infty$, the NCE estimator $\hat{\theta}_T$ converges in probability to the true parameter $\theta^*$ (and $\hat{c}_T$ converges to $\log Z(\theta^*)$), provided that $p_n$ has support wherever $p_d$ does and $\nu \geq 1$.

nodes.name: NCE as nonlinear logistic regression
nodes.statement: NCE is equivalent to logistic regression on the log-density-ratio $G(\mathbf{x}; \theta) = \log p_m(\mathbf{x}; \theta) - \log p_n(\mathbf{x})$ with data and noise as the two classes. The optimal classifier satisfies $G^*(\mathbf{x}) = \log p_d(\mathbf{x}) - \log p_n(\mathbf{x})$, which recovers $p_d$.

nodes.name: Fixed noise distribution limitation
nodes.statement: The noise distribution $p_n$ is fixed throughout training. As the model $p_m$ improves and approaches $p_d$, the classification task becomes harder and the gradient signal weakens. This slows learning when $p_m$ is already close to $p_d$ on a subset of the data space.

nodes.name: Avoids partition function computation
nodes.statement: Unlike maximum likelihood (which requires computing or approximating $Z(\theta)$), NCE treats $\log Z$ as an additional parameter and learns it jointly. The computational cost is $O(\nu)$ model evaluations per data point, independent of the cost of computing $Z$.
